mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen for three consecutive weeks (3.7 -> 0.6 -> -4.4 -> -13.3), indicating strong negative momentum in discretionary outings. This trend persists via habituation and reduced social routines, pulling the next-4-week mean further below the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically over last 4 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages higher than the last 28 days despite the monotonic 4-week decline, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (4.9 -> 7.7 -> 6.4 -> 9.3) combined with falling RETAIL_REC suggests a substitution effect where people shift time spent at home away from retail and recreation trips. When RESIDENTIAL rises while RETAIL_REC falls in the same week, the substitution intensifies, driving further RETAIL_REC decline over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week by more than 2 points while RETAIL_REC falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 4.9 to 9.3 while RETAIL_REC fell from 3.7 to -13.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds upward in the next 2 weeks while RESIDENTIAL continues to climb, the substitution interaction is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS (-4.4 to -16.7) combined with TRANSIT falling to -8.7 signals tightening mobility restrictions or public caution, which historically precedes continued suppression of retail and recreation visits as restrictions bite into commercial activity.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 and TRANSIT falls below -5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached -16.7 and TRANSIT reached -8.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next week despite PARKS and TRANSIT breaching these thresholds, the policy-tightening mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains persistently elevated (53.7 down to 48.9, still far above baseline) even as RETAIL_REC collapses, suggesting a seasonal essential-shopping pattern (e.g., holiday stockpiling) that substitutes for discretionary retail visits. This seasonal split is expected to persist short-term, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above 48 while RETAIL_REC fell to -13.3
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM declines toward baseline while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, the seasonal substitution explanation is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has oscillated sharply (-4.3, -14.9, 6.0, -0.6) while TRANSIT has steadily declined, indicating unstable commuting patterns combined with reduced transit use. The interaction of volatile workplace attendance and falling transit suppresses incidental retail trips linked to commuting, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung between -14.9 and 6.0 while TRANSIT fell from 3.3 to -8.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite continued WORKPLACES volatility and TRANSIT decline, the commuting-interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT decline exceeding 5 points (as seen from -2.6 to -8.7) often marks a crossing into stricter mobility regimes, which mechanically reduces access to retail districts, producing a short-horizon drop in RETAIL_REC the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -2.6 to -8.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a TRANSIT drop greater than 5 points, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near 48-49 for the last two weeks after an initial decline, suggesting behavioral equilibrium has been reached. In such steady-state conditions, retail and recreation mobility tends to mean-revert upward after a sharp dip, as pent-up discretionary demand resumes.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varied only 48.6-48.9 over last 2 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, the mean-reversion hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined in near lockstep with RETAIL_REC over the last 3 weeks (both trending negative), indicating a shared outdoor/discretionary-activity suppression driver. This co-movement is expected to continue, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -4.4 to -16.7 while RETAIL_REC fell from 3.7 to -13.3 over same period
failure_condition: If PARKS and RETAIL_REC decouple such that PARKS keeps falling while RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks, the co-movement mechanism fails.
